title: Count the Vowels
oneLiner: Walk through a string one character at a time and count the ones that are vowels, ignoring case.
keyTakeaway: Looping over a string gives you its characters one by one. Normalise case once (lowercase the character) and test membership in a small set of allowed characters, instead of writing ten separate comparisons.
explanation:
Return how many vowels (a, e, i, o, u, upper or lower case) a string contains. "y" doesn't count. An empty string has 0.

Loop over the characters with foreach (char c in text) or for c in text. For each one, turn it to lowercase (char.ToLower(c) in C#, c.lower() in Python) and check whether it's one of the vowels: "aeiou".Contains(...) in C#, ... in "aeiou" in Python. Keep a counter that starts at 0.

Once that works, try a one-liner: text.Count(c => "aeiouAEIOU".Contains(c)) with LINQ in C#, or sum(1 for c in text.lower() if c in "aeiou") in Python.

visualizationSteps.message: Count the vowels in "Pump On". Start the count at 0.
'u' lowercases to 'u', which is in "aeiou": count is now 1.
'O' lowercases to 'o', which is in "aeiou": count is now 2.

complexity.note: Each of the n characters is checked once against a fixed set of five vowels; only a counter is stored.
